sentences.text: Acondylacanthus is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish belonging to the family Ctenacanthidae within the order Ctenacanthiformes.
This group includes eleven described species, such as A. gracilis and A. jaekeli.
There are ten recorded fossil occurrences of Acondylacanthus in the Paleobiology Database.
The genus is defined solely by isolated dorsal fin spines, leading to uncertainty about whether it is synonymous with tooth-based genera.
The genus lived from the Eifelian to the Wuchiapingian, spanning from 393.47 to 254.14 million years ago.
Most species are known from Carboniferous deposits in America and the British Isles.
The species A. jaekeli is found in the upper Frasnian of Germany and the Upper Famennian of Russia.
